source_quality.notes: pages 11 and 18 lost from the text layer; equations read from the raster

task_reconstruction: Measure the effect of the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse, score a bus rapid transit corridor, and choose a mix of bus lanes, walking infrastructure and micro-mobility hubs.

section_map.summary: summary of the three models and the three aims
background, the collapse, and the restated problem
the nine data files and the cleaning rules
the four-tuple road network and its metrics
the collapse, the equilibrium assignment and the fuzzy score
the multimodal network and the bus rapid transit corridor

contributions.summary: the bridge capacity set to zero at the collapse and the flow reassigned at equal travel time
a four-factor score weighted by the entropy of past incidents
a bus corridor scored on mode share, inequality and emissions
a three-objective program calibrated on other cities

dependency_graph.relation: the efficiency and the redistributed flow are two of the four factors
the road graph is extended with bus, walking and transfer edges
the mode shares and the accessibility feed the three objectives

assumptions.summary: the network covers the main roads and ignores the minor branches
edge weights stay fixed within each year
one value of time stands for a whole group

data_and_preprocessing.summary: nine competition files plus counts from the state road map
outliers fenced at three standard deviations and replaced by the mean
missing numeric values replaced by the mean and missing text filled with zeros
side-road counts transferred from the main roads with a decay of 0.9

models.summary: four-tuple road network with density, utilization and node balance
four-factor fuzzy score with entropy weights
bus, walk and car network with a nested logit and a Gini coefficient
three-objective program over bus lanes, walking quality and hub density

verification.summary: the score checked against a Markov simulation, error stated as 8.724 percent
the rerouting compared with regional counters, R squared reported as 0.894
the load pushed past a stated share of capacity to find the collapse point

results_trace.summary: bypass flow rises and six corridors pass 85 percent of capacity
the corridor lifts the bus share and lowers the inequality
the case reports a welfare gain and a benefit-cost ratio above one

writing_logic.summary: the summary names the three aims before any method
each assumption is stated and then given its reason
each damage figure is followed by the group it hits
the close names the strands joined, the result, then the next work

language_observations.summary: opens on a three-way balance and a purpose clause
a concession comes before the weights are frozen
the score is introduced by what it quantifies
the close uses an advances-by-integrating clause

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 4 draws the Baltimore network with the bridge marked
Figure 5 draws the traffic in six panels across three years
Figure 8 and Table 4 give the corridor before and after
Figure 13 plots the posterior of the calibrated parameters

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: tying each damage figure to a named group matches a stakeholder brief
owning the static network and the missing behaviour reads as honest rather than weak

weaknesses.summary: the side-road counts are filled by a decay of 0.9 with no justification
the static network misses flow that changes with the hour and the season
differences in what people want and can afford are left out
a straight-line utility may miss how people really choose

independent_extensions.summary: study a lost link by setting its capacity to zero and reassigning the flow
weight a multi-factor score by the entropy of past incidents

unresolved_questions: the travel-time function inside the equilibrium integral is never stated
the entropy weight divides by the logarithm of four while the incident sum runs over an unspecified index
the recovery curve and the stated error are given with no displayed fit
the side-road decay of 0.9 is not derived
the Markov chain reports no length and no acceptance rate
